sections.h2: Ways to sell a Spring Hill house
sections.html:
You can hire a realtor, sell by yourself, or take a cash offer. Which fits depends on how much repair work and waiting you can stomach. Listing means showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval. Cash cuts the bank out, a good match for an inherited house, a rental with a tenant or a home needing repairs.

Spring Hill lies about 30 miles south of Nashville and had an estimated 61,336 people by July 2025, up 21.0 percent since 2020. Owner-occupied homes were worth a median $493,800 for 2020 to 2024, and owners lived in 73.4 percent. Weigh a listing price, minus commission and repairs, against a cash figure, particularly when a mortgage balance or a tax bill is pressing.

Spring Hill straddles Maury and Williamson counties, which means two trustees, two assessors and two sets of rates. The city rate matches on both sides, and the city bills its own tax apart from either county. Learn which county holds your parcel before requesting a payoff.

Who bills what on a Spring Hill house
ChargeRate or detailCollected by
City of Spring Hill tax$0.739 for each $100 assessed, in both countiesCity of Spring Hill, 199 Town Center Parkway
Williamson County tax, Spring Hill area, 2026$1.27 per $100, for a combined $2.009Williamson County Trustee
Maury County taxRate set after the 2026 countywide reassessmentMaury County Trustee, One Public Square, Columbia

State law sets the assessment at 25 percent of value. The Maury Trustee can give the current Maury rate.

Williamson County mails statements in early October, with payment open from the first Monday of October until February 28 the next year. From March 1, 1.5 percent interest builds on the first of every month. The Williamson Trustee cannot waive, prorate or release tax or interest. Maury County takes payments at One Public Square in Columbia between 8 and 4, by drop box or mail, and online for a 2.5 percent vendor charge.

The city has its own schedule. Delinquent city tax picks up penalty and interest totaling 1.5 percent a month once February ends, and 2025 taxes not paid before April 1, 2027 pass to the Clerk and Master of the relevant county, after which the city cannot take payment. For relief or the tax freeze, call the city's property tax clerk at (629) 241-8301 and book an appointment. Statements go to the January 1 owner of record, so a seller who has already closed should forward the bill to the new owner.

sections.h2: Sewer capacity and your buyer's plans
sections.html:
The city agreed to a moratorium under TDEC Consent Order WPC2025-0093, and the Board of Mayor and Aldermen passed Ordinance 25-29 on January 5, 2026, creating a framework for the sewer capacity that remains. It keeps the city in compliance with the order, stops further allocation beyond what the system can handle and gives a predictable way to share what is left. Projects or tenant spaces that receive allocation must install flow meters.

Selling an existing house, you will notice this mostly with buyers who plan to build, add on or divide a lot. Ask city planning staff, at planning@springhilltn.org or 931-486-2252, whether a parcel has sewer allocation before promising any buyer that plans can go forward.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or an inherited house
sections.html:
Most Spring Hill sellers live in the house, but rentals and inherited properties still turn up regularly. A tenant means you should pull the lease, rent and end date. An inherited house means locating the deed and asking the right county's trustee for a payoff first.

Cash buyers can take the property occupied or vacant and need no bank sign-off, which helps when taxes are running or heirs are splitting the money.

Buyers using a mortgage normally face an appraisal, an inspection and repair talks, any of which can reopen the price. Cash buyers pay for the house in its present state, so timing hinges on clearing title and getting payoffs from the two tax offices.

Whichever offer you take, keep the written payoffs from the city and the county with your closing papers.

sections.h2: Papers a Spring Hill seller needs
sections.html:
• Your deed, which identifies the county that holds the land records.
  • A loan statement, so the payoff can be requested early.
  • Written payoffs from the city and from the county trustee.
  • Leases for any tenant, and any short-term rental permit.
  • Permit records for past additions, available through city planning.

Calls to City Hall at 931-486-2252 and to the right county trustee early in the process tend to surface problems while there is still time to solve them.

Running a Spring Hill house as a vacation rental requires a city permit. The application fee is $150 for an owner-occupied short-term rental and $300 for any other type. Permits last one year and must be renewed after safety and property inspections and payment of fees. Applicants email the packet to planning@springhilltn.org with these items:

  • Hotel-motel tax certificates, where they apply under T.C.A. 67-4-1401
  • The code compliance form from the city's business license page
  • A floor plan with the emergency evacuation route, plus a dimensioned site plan showing parking and guest access
  • Proof of insurance, a trash plan and a description of cleaning and maintenance
  • The days of operation, whether all year, holidays, or weekends

An investor looking at a Spring Hill house should ask the planning office whether an existing permit carries over to a new owner, because the application names the property owner and agent.

The realty transfer tax runs $0.37 per $100 of price, and the state revenue department puts it on the grantee, the buyer. It is paid at the Register of Deeds in the county, Maury or Williamson, that keeps the parcel's land records. Back taxes come out of proceeds, and the title company asks both the county trustee and the city for payoffs.

Before saying yes to an offer:

  • Identify the county and ask each office for a written payoff.
  • Check the city planning office about permits for past additions.
  • Gather the deed, loan statement and any tenant leases.
  • Confirm the school zone, either Maury County Public Schools or the Williamson County School District, for a buyer's questions.

City Hall is at 199 Town Center Parkway, and its main line is 931-486-2252.

faqs.q: Which county is Spring Hill in?
faqs.a: Both. Spring Hill lies in Maury and Williamson counties, so a house can have either county's trustee and school district. The city rate is $0.739 per $100 on both sides.

faqs.q: What is the quickest way to sell in Spring Hill?
faqs.a: Cash can close sooner than a listing because it skips lender approval and repair haggling. Check county and city tax payoffs first, since open balances are settled at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Spring Hill property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city rate is $0.739 per $100 of assessed value. In the Williamson County portion, the county rate is $1.27 for 2026, a combined $2.009 per $100. Ask the Maury Trustee for the Maury rate.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent out a Spring Hill home for short stays?
faqs.a: Yes. The permit costs $150 for owner-occupied homes and $300 for other properties, renewed yearly after inspections. Send the application to planning@springhilltn.org.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Spring Hill sale?
faqs.a: The buyer. The state's realty transfer tax is $0.37 for each $100 of price, collected at the Register of Deeds for the parcel's county.
